# Complementing a formula of arbitrary depth

Use the star model of the intersection atlas. A raw signal is a free union of row and column stars. A paid gate intersects two free unions of raw signals and earlier paid gates. The output is another free union. Paid depth counts intersections on a path. A formula pays for each occurrence of a subcomputation. Write C_D(H) and F_D(H) for the minimum circuit and formula cost at paid depth at most D.

**Theorem.** Fix D ≥ 1 and m = 2^(D−1). Among all finite bipartite graphs generated by a formula of at most k paid gates, at any source depth, the worst cost of computing the complement at depth D is Θ_D(2^(k/m)). This holds for both circuit and formula targets. Equality of k-bit strings is an extremal example up to constants: its complement, inequality, has a parallel k-gate formula. Thus arbitrary nesting in a formula does not increase the worst cost by even a factor growing with k.

**Stability.** In a given normalized source formula let t count paid gates that have at least one paid child. For any fixed c > 0, if the depth-D complement costs at least c·2^(k/m), then t is bounded solely in terms of c and D. The bound concerns the number of nonleaf paid gates. One such gate can have many children through free unions. The constants here depend on D. The earlier parallel-source theorem has sharper uniform control as D grows.

**Circuit consequence.** Allow unrestricted reuse and put w equal to the treewidth of the undirected dependency graph of the paid source gates. The endpoints of an edge are a gate and a paid input to one of its arms. If w=o(k), the worst complement cost at fixed D is at most 2^(k/m+o(k)). Any excess of εk in the exponent, for fixed ε>0, requires linear treewidth. If r gates are read more than once (including the final output), the upper bound is also O_D(3^r·2^((k−r)/m)). These assertions concern source wiring. No independence or sparsity of the output graph is required.

For circuits of arbitrary wiring, the [two-layer upper bound](UNRESTRICTED.md) places the worst exponent at most 3/5.

## Separate the source gates

Suppose deletion of s gates partitions the remaining gates into m blocks of sizes b₁,…,bₘ, with no dependency between different blocks. The blocks need not be contiguous in evaluation order. Then the complement has a **formula** of depth at most 1+ceil(log₂ m) and cost at most

    3^s (sum_z 2^b_z + m − 1).

At a rejecting cell every gate demanded false must have a false operand. Mark a separator gate either inactive, or active with a specified false operand. This gives at most 3^s signatures. An inactive mark makes no truth assertion. Its use as a required false gate invalidates the certificate. Demand the output gates and the dependencies of the marked operands. Reject inconsistent marks within the separator. The raw output masks and the masks of the marked operands must all be absent. This is a single rectangle condition.

In each block choose one operand per paid gate. Starting from the demands, follow the chosen operands backwards, including every dependency encountered in the same block. If a required separator gate is inactive, discard this choice. All raw row and column masks encountered must be absent. For fixed local choices and signature these conditions give one rectangle, including the common raw exclusions. Freely union at most 2^b_z rectangles in block z. Intersect all m block tests in a balanced tree, paying m−1 times. Freely union the answers across signatures. Zero-dimensional rectangles, empty blocks, direct raw output stars, and edges going from the separator into a block and back at different places in the topological order are all allowed.

For soundness combine the local active gates with the active separator. Every demanded gate has a specified operand with absent raw signals and only active dependencies. Induction in source order proves all active gates false. Conversely, at any rejecting cell mark all false separator gates and pick a false operand for each false gate. These choices pass every local test. The [Lean factorization](../../../../lean/PEqualNP/PaidDepth/SeparatorComplement.lean) establishes the full row-by-column equivalence, with three states per separator gate and a single binary word per block. It also permits row and column witnesses to use different local active sets: their intersection remains closed under the selected dependencies. Lean uses equal block sizes; padding with unused independent gates is harmless. The construction above counts the sharper individual sizes.

## The discount inside a formula

Normalize each source occurrence by folding free unions into the arms and final output. Discard unused gates. A paid gate is a child of at most one arm occurrence, or is an output root. Thus the paid occurrences form a rooted forest. Raw-only tests can be included directly in the rectangle belonging to a certificate.

Count syntactically different rejecting traces, allowing identical rectangles to be counted more than once. A demanded gate selects one arm and demands every child in that arm. A forest of roots requires every root false. The empty forest contributes one trace, concatenation multiplies counts, and adding a paid root to two operand forests with counts U,V gives U+V traces. Every nonempty forest has at least two syntactic traces. If a root has children, at least one of U,V is ≥2, and both are ≥1. Consequently U+V ≤ (3/2)UV. Always U+V ≤ 2UV. Induction gives

    traces · 4^t ≤ 2^k · 3^t.

The [Lean inequality](../../../../lean/PEqualNP/PaidDepth/FormulaTraceBound.lean) proves this for every triple generated by those three constructors. In particular log₂(traces) ≤ k−t/4, since (4/3)^4 ≥ 2. Constraints imposed by a fixed separator signature can discard traces or add raw exclusions. A component root that is not demanded costs one empty trace. Neither operation increases this bound.

## Balance cost rather than vertex count

Give each nonleaf paid gate weight 3/4 and each leaf weight 1. Total weight W is k−t/4. There is an ordering of the forest in which at any cut at most p=ceil(log₂(t+1))+1 vertices before the cut have a neighbor after it. To see this, order isolated paid roots first. On the forest induced by the t internal vertices, take a centroid in each component, list it first, and recurse on its remaining components consecutively. A centroid exists by walking to a neighboring component of more than half the mass until none remains. Each recursive component has at most half as many vertices. Only ancestors of the current recursion can cross a cut. Insert the original leaf children of each internal vertex immediately after it. This adds at most the current parent to a frontier.

Cut this ordering when cumulative weight first reaches jW/m, for j=1,…,m−1. Empty blocks are allowed. Each block has weight at most W/m+1. Remove the union S of the frontiers at these cuts. Its size s is at most (m−1)p, and it separates the blocks. A surviving original internal vertex that becomes a leaf must have lost a child in S. Distinct parents cannot lose the same child. Therefore in each block the local trace bound is at most 2^(W/m+1+s/4). In using this count, an interior child whose parent is still in its block can never be demanded independently by a separator or the output: the source is a formula. This is where the single-use hypothesis enters.

The complete target formula costs at most

    3^s (m·2^(W/m+1+s/4) + m−1).

For fixed m this is at most K_m·2^(k/m)·(t+2)^{a_m}·2^(−t/(4m)), with finite constants K_m and a_m independent of k,t. The last two factors have bounded product, tending to zero as t grows. This proves the upper bound and stability. Equality supplies the matching lower bound from the [previous paid-depth theorem](../THEOREM.md): the positive diagonal on 2^k labels forces Ω_D(2^(k/m)) gates, including against arbitrary reuse. The one-layer source for inequality is the bitwise-mismatch construction of Cavalar and Oliveira.

## Arbitrary source wiring

For a graph of treewidth w, every induced subgraph with N vertices admits a separator bag of at most w+1 vertices leaving components of size at most N/2. Assign each vertex to one containing bag in a tree decomposition of width w. Take a centroid bag for these weights. Connectedness of the bags carrying each vertex and coverage of every edge give the separation after deleting that bag. Recursively listing separator bags first, with their components consecutive, gives a vertex frontier of size at most (w+1)(2+ceil(log₂(max(1,k/(w+1))))): stop when the component fits into one bag's vertex budget and list it directly. Old components already finished have no surviving edges to later ones except through listed ancestor bags.

Take m blocks of size at most ceil(k/m) before deleting their cut frontiers. Apply the separator construction. For fixed m, the additive overhead in the base-two logarithm of the cost is O_m((w+1)(1+log₂(max(1,k/(w+1))))). It is o(k) for any w=o(k), including widths close to linear. This proves the stated necessary condition for a strictly greater limiting exponent. An expander-shaped dependency graph on its own gives no semantic lower bound.

For the second bound, first condition on the r gates with multiple occurrences as operands or outputs. In a fixed valid signature the surviving paid dependencies form a singly used forest. A required input of an active separator arm is a forest root or another separator. A local arm that requires an inactive separator cannot justify rejection. The preceding certificate construction and trace inequalities hold with these fixed rejections or prohibitions; the latter can equivalently be encoded by a universal raw strip on the prohibited arm. Absorb common row and column exclusions into the first-layer rectangles. Applying the formula upper bound to the k−r remaining gates for each signature proves the stated 3^r estimate. In particular at depth two a lower bound of 2^((1/2+ε)k) would require at least (εk−O(1))/(log₂3−1/2) multiply used paid gates in any k-gate presentation.

## Scope and credit

Pudlák, Rödl and Savický developed graph complexity. Cavalar and Oliveira established the exact intersection cost for inequality (Proposition 40 in their paper). This work uses pjscruggs’s row/column star convention and the existing equality depth lower bound linked above. The new upper bound treats arbitrary-depth input formulas and arbitrary source circuits with separators. Separator methods for ordinary Boolean circuits and for knowledge compilation are established prior work. Their target models and depth measures differ. Historical priority for these particular star-model bounds is unestablished.
